A1.justification: Both PDFs describe InkSight and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices. Content can be reliably matched across the revised title, pagination and appendix numbering.

before.justification: v3 reports original benchmark results, ablations, a human evaluation on 200 HierText samples, and experiments training handwriting recognizers with derendered data.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results and adds GPU throughput measurements and further full-page derendering examples.

M1.justification: Appendix J adds a conditional inference fallback: if Recognize and Derender produces empty ink, inference is repeated using Vanilla Derender. The architecture, tokenizer and training objectives remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish that retained benchmark results were recomputed with this fallback.

E1.justification: Appendix B adds Korean handwriting evaluation examples in Figures 38–40, extending the represented scripts beyond v3's examples. Training datasets and the IAM, IMGUR5K, HierText and IAMOnDB evaluation coverage remain unchanged; the German, neon-sign and sand examples discussed in the new Appendix K already existed.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparator sets are unchanged. Both versions use GVS Line Drawing Vectorization for handwriting, Sketch Simplification for sketches, and compare the same three GVS variants and input treatments in Appendix H.

E3.justification: Appendix G introduces a throughput benchmark on Titan RTX, T4 and V100 GPUs, measuring tokens per second with greedy decoding and batch size 32. Existing benchmark splits, metrics, training budgets and human-evaluation procedures are unchanged.

E4.justification: Figures 35–40 add full-page case studies, including evidence about generalization to Korean handwriting absent from Small-p's training. Existing augmentation, recognition-task, inference-mode and frozen-ViT ablations, along with the open-ended-generation probe, are retained.

E5.justification: The new GPU benchmark explicitly reports averages over five runs, without dispersion estimates. Existing three-seed ablation reporting and human-evaluation inter-rater reliability are unchanged; there is no reported increase in runs for those retained experiments.

E6.justification: Appendix G adds mean throughput results of 114.43 tokens/s for Titan RTX, 47.14 for T4 and 139.14 for V100. New full-page outputs include the Korean example, interpreted as showing weaker Small-p generalization. Tables 2, 3 and 8 and the human-evaluation results retain their numerical values.

T1.justification: The digital-ink representation, normalization and 2N + 3 token-vocabulary definition in Section 3.3 remain unchanged. Neither version adds or removes theoretical propositions, proofs or substantive mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: Introduction contribution 3 drops the explicit claim that the approach is robust 'well beyond its training data,' modestly narrowing that contribution's stated scope. The central claims about photo derendering, reading and writing priors, partial sketch generalization and the public model release remain.

C2.justification: Appendices J and K add explicit qualifications about unseen scripts, ineffective text conditioning and the limitations of the decoding fallback. Appendix O adds discussion of handwriting-related bias and potential geometric pseudo-label applications. Much of the discussion of stroke width, component scaling and frozen-ViT tradeoffs restates existing interpretations.

D1.justification: v4 adds GPU benchmarking details, documents the inference fallback, and supplies a citation where the online-recognizer reference was anonymized. It also adds a project-page link while retaining the existing code and model links. The GPU benchmark does not identify the tested model variant or workload.

R1.justification: The introduction and references add Nuwa as another hardware-based handwriting digitization solution. The related-work discussion and Appendix D's survey of trajectory-recovery approaches otherwise retain their research positioning and cited methods.

P1.justification: v4 revises the title to emphasize teaching vision-language models, rewrites introductory motivation, organizes the expanded appendix discussions with descriptive headings, adds acknowledgments and replaces the appendix outline with a contents list. Most method and experimental prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: Appendix B gains six figures showing three model outputs for each of two additional photographs. v4 also relocates Figure 2, combines the human-evaluation interface and examples on one page, adds publication headers, and clarifies Figure 1's stroke-order caption. Existing result displays are largely retained.

improvement.justification: v4 improves practical transparency through throughput measurements and the documented inference fallback, while the Korean examples and expanded limitations better qualify generalization. These gains are limited: the main empirical results are unchanged, the new cases are selective, and the throughput benchmark remains underspecified. The evidence supports a modest overall quality improvement.
